items.q: Do I need any prior experience with coaching?
items.a: Not at all. Whether you have done therapy, coaching, meditation, other personal development experiences or none, the programme is designed to meet you exactly where you are.

items.q: What is the difference between coaching and therapy?
items.a: Coaching and therapy have different purposes. Coaching is generally focused on where you are now, where you want to go and what may help you move towards it. We may look at the past for context and understanding, but our work is primarily about creating awareness, choices and movement in your present and future.

items.q: How long is a coaching session?
items.a: I typically have one-hour sessions every two weeks. The time in between sessions is an important part of the process, giving you the opportunity to test things out, notice what happens and experience some of the dynamics we have discussed.

items.q: How long is a coaching programme?
items.a: It depends on your objectives, what is going on in your life and where you are in your own self-discovery journey. We will discuss what makes sense for your situation.

items.q: When do I pay for my sessions?
items.a: Payment is due at least 24 hours before each session.

items.q: What happens if I cannot make it to a session or need to reschedule?
items.a: You can reschedule or cancel your session free of charge up to 24 hours before the agreed time. Cancellations or changes with less than 24 hours' notice will be considered a session, unless otherwise agreed.

bioSections.heading: Where I am from and Where I Have Been
paragraphs: I am Italian, married to a Dutch guy. I lived in the Netherlands for 17 years before moving back to Italy in 2026, although we still spend a lot of time there.
After university, I lived and worked in London for over a year to improve my English and experience life abroad.

bioSections.heading: What I Have Studied
paragraphs: I have a master's degree in psychology from the University of Rome "La Sapienza".

When I crossed paths with Unilever, I was fascinated by its international environment, people and values. I ended up spending 20 years there, learning a great deal about leadership, organisations and human behaviour.
In 2017 I decided to bring my psychology background back into my work and specialise in Life Coaching, training in the Co-Active and ORSC models.

bioSections.heading: Where I Have Worked
paragraphs: I opened my private coaching practice in 2020, while still working in Marketing at Unilever.

Unilever's strong focus on people and mental health gave me the opportunity to coach individuals and teams internally and to run mental health and purpose-related programmes, alongside my private coaching practice.

bioSections.heading: What Gives Me Energy And Joy
paragraphs: My biggest source of energy is meaningful connection with other people. I love creating opportunities to celebrate and spend quality time together.
On my own I find energy in crafting and sewing, usually making things for presents or celebrations, all of which brings me full circle to connection.

sections.heading: I Do Not Give Answers, I Ask Questions
sections.body: This way, when we find the answers together, they really mean something, because they come from you, and who knows you better than yourself?

sections.heading: Your Journey, Your Pace
sections.body: We may peek into the past for reference and background, but our work will focus on the present and on building the future you truly want. The programme will be tailored to what you need, where you want to go and where you are in your self-discovery journey. There will be some gentle pushes, but we will always work at your pace.

sections.heading: Our Relationship Matters
sections.body: Our relationship creates the space, energy and safety for your transformation. We will keep it sacred.

sections.heading: Purpose As Your Compass
sections.body: One of the things we may explore is your Purpose: what matters to you, what gives your life energy and meaning. We can turn it into a simple but powerful statement to guide you when you are faced with a decision: which path feels right when you are standing in your purpose? My own purpose is "to help you find your path to and through Wonderland."
